tool.name: pathotypr split-fastq
tool.description: genotypes raw reads against a marker panel without aligning them
tool.command:
## The sample name is taken from the input filename, so the reads are linked to ## fixed names and the outputs are predictable rather than named after a Galaxy ## dataset id. #if $reads.layout == 'paired' #set $ext = 'fastq.gz' if $reads.fwd.is_of_type('fastqsanger.gz') else 'fastq' ln -s '$reads.fwd' 'sample_R1.$ext' && ln -s '$reads.rev' 'sample_R2.$ext' && #else #set $ext = 'fastq.gz' if $reads.single.is_of_type('fastqsanger.gz') else 'fastq' ln -s '$reads.single' 'sample.$ext' && #end if
pathotypr split-fastq --markers '$markers' --reference '$reference' #if $reads.layout == 'paired' -i 'sample_R1.$ext' -i 'sample_R2.$ext' #else -i 'sample.$ext' --no-auto-paired #end if --output-prefix 'result' --kmer-size $kmer_size --min-depth $min_depth --min-alt-percent $min_alt_percent $nested_classification @THREADS@

param.label: Minimum depth
param.help: Reads required at a marker position before a variant is called.

param.label: Minimum alternate allele frequency (%)
param.help: How much of the depth must carry the alternate allele, in whole percent. Lower this for mixed or low-coverage samples, knowing that it also admits sequencing error.

tool.help:
**What it does**
`pathotypr split-fastq` genotypes a marker panel straight from sequencing reads, with no alignment and no assembly. It builds a diagnostic k-mer for each allele of each marker, streams the reads past a Bloom filter, and counts how many reads carry the reference allele and how many carry the alternate one.
Because it streams, memory does not grow with the number of reads.
Two tables come out:
- **per-marker calls**: position, both alleles, the read counts behind each, the alternate fraction, and the lineage the marker belongs to. - **summary**: the count of hits per lineage and the major lineage call, in the same shape *pathotypr classify* produces, so the two are directly comparable.
**Depth and frequency**
A marker is only called when it has at least *minimum depth* reads and the alternate allele reaches *minimum alternate frequency*. The defaults, 10 reads and 95%, are strict on purpose: they are chosen for a clonal sample. Lower the frequency if you expect mixed infections, and expect more sequencing error to come with it.
.. class:: warningmark
**Indels are skipped here.** A marker whose REF and ALT differ in length is dropped, because short reads across repetitive regions give unreliable k-mer matches for insertions and deletions. Detect those with *pathotypr classify* on an assembly instead.
@MARKER_HELP@
